svg.title: Proposed: file reader / writer interfaces (RFC-88 section 2, Paimon model)
svg.text: Proposed: file reader / writer interfaces (RFC-88 section 2, Paimon model)
Formats read and write one Hudi row type; each engine wraps its own rows. Names are placeholders. Compare writer-reader-today.svg.

svg.text: Parquet file: same bytes from any engine
a view, not a copy (Paimon's FlinkRowData)
same bytes as today, no GenericRecord per record
Formats read and write only HoodieRow; each engine provides two wrappers. N + M classes,
as in Paimon; Iceberg's per (format, engine) FormatModel registry stays N x M by design.
Getters are typed and return canonical values (UTF-8 bytes, unscaled decimals, timestamps in
the column's unit): each conversion is written once per logical type, not per engine x format.
The physical schema comes only from FormatSchemaMapper; ValueWriters are chosen from it.
Readers take a SchemaTransformPlan and an optional Hudi Expression.
Engine batch readers stay behind VectorizedFileReader and must match the row reader.
Why: resolves the notes in writer-reader-today.svg
Format holes close: every engine wrapper works with every FileFormatIO.
One writer per format, built from toPhysicalSchema(): three Parquet and two Lance write
No GenericRecord per record on log blocks, ORC writes, Hive or Trino reads; payload
merging keeps Avro (record merger API, outside this design).
FileFormats keys on file format only; a gap is a missing implementation, not a runtime throw.
Batch readers stay (vinothchandar's review), bound to the same plan.
Native (v2) logs already work this way; FileWriter with an OutputStream makes it the rule.
